text.ctx.notation:
Write your post in Markdown as your final reply; the system records it on the board. Don't run commands or change any files.
- Only the Owner can call people in: an @ you write is plain text and wakes nobody. If you want someone's view, say so to the Owner (e.g. "suggest asking XX").
- For something only the Owner and the Lead should see, wrap it in <private owner>…</private>.
- If you have nothing to add, reply [PASS].
Keep the board to conclusions and key points; put detailed material in the workspace and link to it.

text.init.usage:
Usage:
  init.sh new       [dir] [-n name] [--no-now] [--lang zh|en]   install the workbench (AGENTS.md + collab/) in a project, register it with the board and print its URL; with NOW enabled, also add a row to the NOW task table (--no-now skips that)
  init.sh lang      zh|en [dir]   switch the project language: rules and templates in that language, card section titles and field names rewritten by code, config.json updated, then flow render; content is untouched
  init.sh protocol  [dir]   update collab/protocol.md from the latest workbench (keeping "Project notes"), every _template.md and the PROGRESS "Loading map"
  init.sh hook      [dir]   install the Claude Code Stop hook in an existing project: check collab/ at the end of every turn and hand errors back to Claude (new does this automatically)
  init.sh open      [dir] [--print]   open this project on the board if it's running (--print only prints the URL); otherwise say how to start it
  init.sh now       <dir>   set up the NOW dashboard (optional: summarizes several projects, adds schedules and other personal modules; NOW.md + the NOW/ data folder)
  init.sh register  [dir] [-n name]   register an existing workbench project with the board; with NOW enabled, add it back to the NOW task table
  init.sh unregister [dir] [-m one-line result] [--drop]   remove it from the board registry; with NOW enabled, move it from the task table to "Done" (--drop deletes the row); project files and collab/ are untouched
  init.sh team      [team dir]   create your team.json from the example
  init.sh team-sync [dir] [--all] [--force]   regenerate collab/members.md from team.json; --all refreshes every project in the registry and the NOW task table
  init.sh module list | enable <id> | disable <id> | init <id> [--now-dir <NOW data dir>]   manage board modules; enable and disable re-merge the commands
  init.sh tidy      [dir] [--all]   move old collab/ history folders into collab/internal/ (then run init.sh migrate)
  init.sh rules     [--now-dir <NOW data dir>]   merge the core and enabled modules' commands into commands.md in the NOW data folder
  init.sh migrate   [dir] [--dry-run] [--lang zh|en]   migrate an old-format ledger to format 3; backs up to .collab-backup/<time>/ first and can be rerun
  init.sh migrate --rollback [dir]   restore from the latest backup
  init.sh migrate-now [NOW data dir] [--dry-run] [--rollback]   give NOW data files and the team folder their English names
Language: --lang, else COLLAB_LANG, else "lang" in the NOW config.json, else en.

text.rules.head:
# Commands

Generated by `init.sh rules` from the enabled modules ({used}); don't edit by hand. To change a command, edit `core/commands.{lang}.md` in the toolkit or a module's `commands.{lang}.md`, then rerun `init.sh rules` after publishing.

Each command also works when said in Chinese (the names in `commands.zh.md`).

text.talent.intro: Find people by role: each role lists its skills, what it's best at, and which command-line members can play it. The team page shows the members you actually use today; this page is about the capabilities themselves.
text.talent.later: How roles are divided, how skills are described and how this connects to the team are still to be decided.
text.talent.sample: You're looking at example data (core/team-example/talent.json in the toolkit); put your own talent pool in talent.json in the team folder and it will show here.
text.team.capability_intro: The Owner sets the tiers; the Lead uses them under the "picking people" rule. Different models of the same app get their own rows. Tiers: A for hard or critical work (architecture, tricky problems, external deliverables, key reviews); B for medium work; C for simple work (tidying, formatting, batch jobs, looking things up). Cost only needs to be relative.

text.team.dispatcher: Command-line members are dispatched and resumed with the dispatch script: `python3 {path}` ("dispatch" below). Session IDs are recorded automatically in `{runs}`; dispatch checks the task card and goal stages first, and meetings use `dispatch meet`.

text.team.intro: Maintained by the Owner, who is you. Seats (Lead, Executor, tester, Reviewer and so on) are assigned per task or goal stage; this table only lists the seat each member usually takes. Before dispatching, read the "Wake" line in that member's section.
